description: Known-good AI disclosure policy pages, used as a regression fixture for web_crawler.py. If crawl_organization_sync() / probe_known_paths() stops finding these, a scoring/keyword/path change broke recall. All entries in 'orgs' were verified live (fetched + scored with the actual scoring code, not just eyeballed) during the 2026-07-31 refinement pass; the original 3 (apache, trustedfirmware, openinfra) are from the prior session.

orgs.notes: ASF Generative Tooling Guidance - AI-generated content disclosure in contributions
Trusted Firmware AI Policy - Assisted-by: commit token guidance
OpenInfra Foundation Policy for AI Generated Content

Linux Foundation Generative AI Policy - license compliance, third-party copyright, employer-policy compliance for AI-assisted contributions. Found via KNOWN_POLICY_PATHS entry '/legal/generative-ai', score 35.

Eclipse 'Generative AI Usage Guidelines for Committers' - note the probed path '/projects/guidelines/genai/' redirects into a single giant Project Handbook page (~460KB of text) at this URL; the genai section is deep in the page, not at the top, so the crawler's text_snippet (first 1800 chars) captures handbook front matter rather than the genai guidance itself. Score 39, matched via 'ai disclosure', 'assisted-by', 'disclose the use of ai'. Worth revisiting snippet extraction (extract text near the matched phrase instead of always the page start) if Groq verification rejects this one for looking generic.
LLVM AI Tool Use Policy - human-in-the-loop requirement, hosted on their Sphinx docs site (not GitHub). Found via KNOWN_POLICY_PATHS entry '/docs/AIToolPolicy.html', score 35.

Rocky Linux AI-Assisted Contribution Policy, explicitly based on Fedora's. Lives on the docs.rockylinux.org SUBDOMAIN, not rockylinux.org itself - found via the new DOC_SUBDOMAIN_PREFIXES + SUBDOMAIN_PROBE_PATHS probing added this session. Score 52, highest of the new batch.
CPython devguide 'Guidelines for using AI tools'. Lives on devguide.python.org SUBDOMAIN. Score 16 - lowest of the new batch but still 2x MIN_SCORE.
ESLint AI Usage Policy - dedicated policy page on eslint.org itself. Found via KNOWN_POLICY_PATHS entry '/docs/latest/contribute/ai-policy', score 37.
NumPy AI Policy - dedicated page on numpy.org. Also reachable at /doc/stable/dev/ai_policy.html (both in KNOWN_POLICY_PATHS now). Score 18.

WordPress AI Guidelines handbook page. Lives on make.wordpress.org SUBDOMAIN. IMPORTANT: make.wordpress.org 429-rate-limits bursts of concurrent requests (observed live while testing this entry - most of a 20-worker burst against it came back 429), which is why _probe_one_path now retries once after a 1.5s backoff on 429. Score 27.

Taylor & Francis AI Policy (academic publisher, not a software org - included as a structural template: requires authors to name the specific AI tool, version, and reason for use). Found via KNOWN_POLICY_PATHS entry '/our-policies/ai-policy/', score 45. Note: several other KNOWN_POLICY_PATHS entries on this site (e.g. '/legal/ai-policy', '/policy/ai') redirect to the same canonical URL, so probe_known_paths() returns duplicate hits for it when called directly (crawl_organization_sync() dedupes these by final URL; probe_known_paths() alone does not - cosmetic only, not a scoring bug).

known_limitations.description: Real AI disclosure pages found during research that the crawler currently CANNOT reliably find, and why - documented here instead of the 'orgs' regression list so the test suite doesn't assert something the crawler structurally can't do yet. Revisit if the underlying blocker gets addressed.

entries.reason: docs.fedoraproject.org serves an Anubis anti-bot JS challenge ('Making sure you're not a bot!') to plain requests.get() - confirmed live, the page body is the challenge page, not the policy text. Would need a JS-executing headless browser (e.g. Playwright) to get past Anubis's proof-of-work check; out of scope for the requests-based direct prober. Rocky Linux's docs site (same underlying policy, same doc-platform style) is NOT behind Anubis and IS found successfully - see the 'rockylinux' entry above.

Page is real and live but is a thin stub ('GitLab team members should be familiar with the General Purpose AI Tool Usage Requirements here') whose 'here' link points to https://internal.gitlab.com/... - an internal-only URL, not publicly readable. Scores 0: there's no actual policy content on the public page to match against. GitLab's public Acceptable Use Policy (https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/legal/acceptable-use-policy/) does contain one relevant clause ('to falsely represent that output generated by our AI-powered services was solely human-generated') but scores only 3 - it's a general acceptable-use policy where AI is one clause among many unrelated ones (spam, illegal content, etc.), not a dedicated AI disclosure page. Forcing either to pass threshold would require loosening scoring in a way that risks false positives elsewhere; not attempted.

Real content, scores 54 when fetched directly (well above threshold) - but it's a corporate blog post at an unpredictable slug, not a conventional policy path, so KNOWN_POLICY_PATHS direct probing can't find it without knowing the URL in advance. Would only be discoverable via the Scrapy deep-crawl stage finding a link to it from redhat.com's blog index within depth 5 / 100 pages - not verified either way this session (Scrapy stage not exercised for this org).
